# AMD ROCm Policy Replication Topic

This topic is designed for learners who wish to perform embodied policy training, closed loop evaluation, and simulation migration on AMD GPUs. The content starts with ROCm device inspection, MuJoCo data collection, and LeRobot policy training, and extends to RoboCasa365, DexJoCo, DISCOVERSE, RoboWits, and Unitree G1. Each experiment provides input, execution commands, output directories, and evaluation metrics.

## Learning Entry

Just choose a route based on the target, and there is no need to read from start to end according to the file number.

| Route | Suitable for readers | Recommended order | Final output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| grasping policy training | First-time training of robot policy on AMD device | 00 → 01 → 07 → 08/09/10 → 11 → 02 | dataset, model, per-round results, and video |
| policy diagnosis | Existing models, aiming to identify closed loop failures | 02 → 03/04/05 → 06 | stage statistics, action curves, and repair records |
| multi-bench migration | Aiming to reproduce household operations, dexterous hand, and safety control | 09 → 10 → 11/12/13/14/15 → 16 | fixed protocol results, multi-view videos, and archive directories |

When there is no local AMD device, first read [AUP Learning Cloud and AMD Developer Cloud ](00-amd-aup-free-cloud-platform-usage-guide.md). Details on platform web manipulation are provided in [AUP, Jupyter, and Code Server appendix ](appendices/AUP_JUPYTER_CODE_SERVER.md). The main section only retains the environment, storage, and operation steps.

## First Run

1. Confirm the ](01-amd-rocm-device-and-environment-confirmation.md) by using the [ device and environment, and check ROCm, PyTorch, and persistent directories.
2. Open [ pre-trained weights and zero training experience ](08-pre-trained-weights-and-zero-training-experience.md), download a model, or watch the four-view replay in the repository.
3. Perform data collection and training with [ training](07-rocm-end-to-end-collection-training-and-deployment.md), complete teaching collection, data auditing, and short training.
4. Run the batch closed-loop script ](code/README.md) with [ using a fixed random seed, and save `results.jsonl` and videos.
5. Conduct unified evaluation and archiving ](16-unify-the-evaluation-videos-and-result-archiving.md) by following [, and summarize the success rate and operating configurations.

`5000 steps` is the short training configuration for the course. Whether it reaches an usable level is confirmed by the random seed that did not participate in training, physical success determination, and replay video.

## Notebook and Script

- [Notebook description ](notebooks/README.md): Distinguish between readable results, running templates, and end-to-end workflows that depend on upstream projects.
- [Model workflow ](notebooks/workflows/README.md): Separate directories for regular training and protected training to evaluate the models produced during this training.
- [Python script ](code/README.md): Batch closed-loop evaluation, data replay, demonstration videos, and DISCOVERSE data conversion.
- [Upstream project layout ](external/README.md): Place source code, data, models, and running results outside the dedicated catalog.

Notebook is suitable for observing images, states, and actions line by line. Long training, batch evaluation, and batch video recording use script entries, which facilitate restoration and comparison on remote devices.

## Unified Product

At least the following files should be retained for each formal experiment:

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `run_config.json` | Upstream version, model, task, observation, action, camera, and random seed |
| `metrics.jsonl` | Number of training steps, loss, learning rate, time consumption, and device metrics |
| `checkpoints/` | Loadable models and configurations |
| `eval/<task>/eval_info.json` | Per-round results and task success determination |
| `eval/<task>/videos/` | Success and failure replays |
| `summary.json` | Success rate and stage statistics aggregated from per-round results |

Large dataset, models, caches, and batch videos are stored on a persistent disk or a public model repository; the Git repository stores source code, small configurations, short example media, and documentation.
